passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

question.question: What is the final cost after a 20% discount and then 10% tax?

solution.visualShortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order.
solution.explanation: Read the values from the chart and apply the stated operation. Formula: (Σ quantity × unit price) × (1 − discount ÷ 100) × (1 + tax ÷ 100). Report subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 6 × 22 = 132 EUR; exact. Workshop subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 4 × 25 = 100 EUR; exact. Order subtotal: subtotal₁ + subtotal₂; substitute 132 + 100 = 232 EUR; exact. After discount: subtotal × (1 − discount ÷ 100); substitute 232 × (1 − 20 ÷ 100) = 185.6 EUR; exact. Final cost: after discount × (1 + tax ÷ 100); substitute 185.6 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100) = 204 EUR; rounded to nearest whole number. Final result: 204 EUR (rounded to nearest whole number where needed). Option B is correct. Visual shortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order. Each distractor records the specific calculation mistake it makes.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

The missing bottom-right figure must therefore apply both changes. Option E is correct because it applies add a nested shape and cycle the shape. Other options omit one change or use a plausible wrong direction, rotation, fill, or element count.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

solution.visualShortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order.
solution.explanation: Read the values from the chart and apply the stated operation. Formula: (Σ quantity × unit price) × (1 − discount ÷ 100) × (1 + tax ÷ 100). Report subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 6 × 22 = 132 EUR; exact. Workshop subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 4 × 25 = 100 EUR; exact. Order subtotal: subtotal₁ + subtotal₂; substitute 132 + 100 = 232 EUR; exact. After discount: subtotal × (1 − discount ÷ 100); substitute 232 × (1 − 20 ÷ 100) = 185.6 EUR; exact. Final cost: after discount × (1 + tax ÷ 100); substitute 185.6 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100) = 204.2 EUR; rounded to 1 decimal place. Final result: 204.2 EUR (rounded to 1 decimal place where needed). passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

question.question: What is the final cost after a 20% discount and then 5% tax?

solution.visualShortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order.
solution.explanation: Read the values from the chart and apply the stated operation. Formula: (Σ quantity × unit price) × (1 − discount ÷ 100) × (1 + tax ÷ 100). Report subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 6 × 24 = 144 EUR; exact. Workshop subtotal: quantity × unit price; substitute 3 × 34 = 102 EUR; exact. Order subtotal: subtotal₁ + subtotal₂; substitute 144 + 102 = 246 EUR; exact. After discount: subtotal × (1 − discount ÷ 100); substitute 246 × (1 − 20 ÷ 100) = 196.8 EUR; exact. Final cost: after discount × (1 + tax ÷ 100); substitute 196.8 × (1 + 5 ÷ 100) = 206.64 EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. Final result: 206.64 EUR (rounded to 2 decimal places where needed). Option B is correct. Visual shortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order. Each distractor records the specific calculation mistake it makes.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

The missing bottom-right figure must therefore apply both changes. Option D is correct because it applies rotate by 90° and change the fill/shading. Other options omit one change or use a plausible wrong direction, rotation, fill, or element count.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

question.question: Revenue is 8% higher each year. What will it be after 4 years?

solution.visualShortcut: Follow the trend and apply the same multiplier for each additional year.
solution.explanation: Read the values from the table and apply the stated operation. Formula: initial × (1 + rate ÷ 100)^years. Growth factor: 1 + rate ÷ 100; substitute 1 + 8 ÷ 100 = 1.08 factor; exact. After year 1: previous value + (previous value × rate ÷ 100); substitute 275.00 + (275.00 × 8 ÷ 100) = 297 thousand EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.
